text:
Carter Verhaeghe has 22 points in 25 games, and he'd be the first to tell you a lot of them have bounced his way. Florida has scored 11 more goals than its chances deserved with him on the ice, the biggest on-ice luck gap on our flag list, and he's scoring on 19% of his own shots against a 12 to 16% range we'd expect. When that fades, the point pace should come down.

The good news for the Panthers is that the player underneath is still a good one. His last ten games (9 points, 7 of them assists) match the chances he's generating, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 93rd percentile for primary shot assists last season, with 72% of his exits leaving the zone with possession. Evolving-Hockey rated him a play driver against top competition.

He's a three-time Stanley Cup winner from a team that wins on structure and depth. The one odd note: just 13.8 minutes in the win over Ottawa on Tuesday. Worth watching whether that was a game-script blip.
